Subject: Postmortem: hawthorn-7b-v2 elevated 503s/timeouts (closure)

Hi Sarah and Acme team — thank you again for your patience. Below is the high-level postmortem and actions we've completed. Full PDF attached and a canonical doc is on Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HawthornPostmortemDoc

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-11-29 08:05 PT: first error surge observed in hawthorn-7b-v2 for several accounts (including ACME).
- 08:24 PT: internal incident created (INC-20261129-HAW).
- 08:35 PT: ACME traffic routed to hawthorn-7b-v1; autoscale headroom increased.
- 08:48 PT: error rates returned to baseline for ACME.

Root cause: a quantization kernel rollout for hawthorn-7b-v2 introduced a regression in the KV-cache eviction path under high concurrent stream counts. In short, a kernel path that was meant to reduce memory use caused transient cache thrashing and a small set of requests to hit an unhandled error path, resulting in 503s/timeouts.

Remediation & completed actions:
1) Reverted the quantization kernel change on hawthorn-7b-v2 (rolled back at 09:15 PT).
2) Tightened pre-release validation for kernel/quantization rollouts (added KV-cache stress tests to release gating).
3) Increased default KV-cache retention for dedicated pools by +20% as a safety buffer (config change applied).
4) Improved monitoring: added a model-level eviction-rate alert and a synthetic request test that runs every 5m against major variants.
5) Applied a goodwill credit to AcmeCo for the impacted window (Ben will follow up on details).

What you'll see from us:
- Ben Carter (CC) will send a short credit summary and confirm billing impact.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem readout with your SRE/Platform lead if you'd like — propose Thu 12/03 11:00 PT.

If you want any additional artifacts (full traces, kernel diffs), let me know and I'll share the internal bundle. Attached: postmortem-hawthorn7b-20261201.pdf (full RCA).

Apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as a severity-two production bug and the fixes above are in process to reduce recurrence risk.

-Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference
